cheribsd-revocation.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured. CheriBSD's revocation sweeps capabilities to freed heap memory, so the stale pointer SHOULD be revoked and the probe fault -- but only if the sweep has run between the free and the access. The reduction frees and re-allocates immediately, which is the case least favourable to revocation, so a clean reading here is about sweep TIMING and not about the defect. That must be read in-guest before it is called either way.

title: a realloc read one field and stored its result in another, leaving two owners of one block
object: s->thread_buf, one direct allocation, after the realloc also reachable as s->slice_params_buf
lifetime_ender: av_realloc_f(s->thread_buf, ...), which frees s->thread_buf's block when it moves
shape: a realloc whose source and destination fields differ, so one block gets two owners
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct av_malloc-family allocation, with no pool or refstruct layer. FFmpeg's av_malloc is malloc plus alignment.
fidelity: model consumer, real lifetime: the allocation, the free and the later access through the stale pointer are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md. The later access is any use of s->thread_buf, which still holds the released address.
status: built 2026-10-08; native arms measured by runners/run-native.sh in the same commit. The platform arms are declared predictions.
live_proof: absent at the pin: n9.0.1:libavcodec/diracdec.c reallocs `av_realloc_f(s->slice_params_buf, ...)`. The form consuming `s->thread_buf` is at 8a4ea9644833^ and is absent from the pin.
nested_why: the object came straight from av_malloc/av_mallocz/av_malloc_array/av_realloc -- which on the platform is malloc -- with no AVBufferPool, AVRefStructPool or other recycling layer between it and the request. So under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested. Its sibling ../pool-repros holds the nested ones.
distinguishing: the defect is a FIELD CONFUSION rather than a missing clear: the realloc consumes s->thread_buf and publishes the result as s->slice_params_buf, so after it there are two fields naming one block and one of them names the released address. No null assignment would have fixed it -- only naming the right source does.
